title: Business Funding
headline: Funding for the way your business works.
intro: Win the contract, add capacity or take the next growth step. We help you turn the cash requirement into a clear funding conversation, whether or not you know the product name.
summary: A starting point for working capital, business borrowing and acquisitions.
uses: Keep the cash cycle moving
Explore invoice finance, loans and revolving facilities around the gap between outgoing costs and incoming payments.
Invest in the next stage
Separate expansion costs from acquisition funding, and test the resulting repayment plan.
Review existing borrowing
Compare the current commitment with replacement funding, including settlement charges and any changes in security.
steps: Describe the cash need
Explain the business objective, approximate amount and date funds are needed.
Identify the relevant products
Compare borrowing, receivables, stock or asset routes against the actual need.
Agree what happens next
Establish the information and provider approach that make sense for the requirement.
terms: Total cost
Look beyond the headline rate. Understand interest, arrangement and intermediary fees, any exit charges and the assumptions behind a comparison.
Repayments and flexibility
Match payment dates and duration to cash generation. Clarify early repayment, renewals, increases and what happens if trading changes.
Security and guarantees
A provider may require business security or personal guarantees. Requirements vary; understand the specific exposure before committing.
Assessment and timing
A first response is different from approval or drawdown. Information, credit assessment, documentation and any security arrangements affect the timetable.
prepare: What the funding must achieve
Approximate amount, duration and any important deadline
How the business expects to repay and what it already owes
faqs: Can you help if my bank has declined?
The reason for the decision matters. A different provider or structure may consider a different case, but a decline does not establish that funding will be available elsewhere.
Will I need a personal guarantee?
That depends on the provider, structure and assessment. Any proposed guarantee and its implications need to be made clear before a commitment.
Will an enquiry affect my credit file?
An enquiry is not a credit application. The actual assessment process and any proposed credit searches should be explained before they happen.
valueHeading: You bring the business objective. We help frame the funding.
valueIntro: We help organise the requirement and the information behind it, then arrange relevant funding introductions with your agreement. You can start with a business problem rather than a product choice.
enquiryHeading: What does your business need to achieve?
enquiryIntro: Tell us the goal, the cash requirement and your timing. We will help identify a useful starting point.
definition: Business funding is an umbrella for several different requirements. A loan, invoice facility, stock arrangement or equipment agreement each releases cash in a different way. Start with when money leaves the business, when it comes back and what the funding must enable.
definitionHeading: Start with what the money needs to do.
benefitsHeading: Find a route around the business decision.

Invest in capacity
Separate an equipment purchase from hiring, marketing or other expansion costs.
Make a strategic move
Bring acquisition or refinancing requirements into view without assuming one loan is the answer.

title: Bridging Loans
headline: Cover the gap. Keep the next move in sight.
intro: An opportunity cannot always wait for a sale, refinance or other source of capital. Explore short-term business funding around a defined need and a credible repayment plan.
summary: Bridge a temporary business funding gap
uses: Between funding rounds
Explore the gap before an anticipated investment round, with a clear view of investor progress, remaining conditions and alternative repayment options.
Between outgoing costs and incoming cash
Cover a defined timing gap around customer payments, stock, contract delivery or a business transition.
Between an opportunity and completion
Explore temporary funding for an acquisition, property purchase, equipment investment or refinancing while the next source of capital is arranged.
steps: Define the gap
Identify the amount, costs to cover and date funds are required.
Examine the exit
Set out the proposed repayment event, evidence and conditions still outstanding.
Test a delay
Look at fallback options and the cost if the gap lasts longer than planned.
terms: Repayment and delays
Establish what will repay the loan and when. Test what happens if an investment round, sale, payment or refinance is delayed or does not complete.
The full cost
Compare interest over the expected term alongside arrangement, legal, valuation and exit costs where applicable. Understand any minimum interest period and early repayment terms.
Security and guarantees
Requirements depend on the facility and provider. Understand any business or property security, personal guarantees and the consequences of default before agreeing terms.
Terms and conditions
Review repayment dates, covenants and conditions for releasing funds. Extensions and replacement funding should never be assumed.
prepare: The business purpose, approximate amount and date funds are needed
How long the gap is expected to last and the proposed repayment source
The status of any raise, sale, receivable or refinance and its remaining conditions
Existing borrowing, potential security and a fallback if the expected exit changes
faqs: Can a bridging loan cover the gap before another funding round?

That is a requirement we can discuss. The stage of the raise, investor commitments, conditions and alternative repayment options matter. An anticipated round alone does not establish that a loan is available or suitable.
Is bridging only for property?

No. Businesses can need temporary funding for cash flow, transactions and funding transitions as well as property. The appropriate facility depends on the purpose, repayment source and provider assessment.
How much can we borrow, and how quickly?
The amount, term, cost and timing depend on the business, facility and provider. We start with your requirement and deadline; availability and completion cannot be confirmed before assessment.
valueHeading: Get clear on the need, the timing and the exit.
valueIntro: We help explain the temporary requirement and identify which provider conversations are relevant. A real deadline helps focus the work; it does not remove the need for assessment or guarantee completion.
enquiryHeading: What does your business need to bridge?
enquiryIntro: Tell us the gap, approximate amount, deadline and expected repayment source. We will start with the situation, not ask you to assume a particular structure.
definition: Bridging covers a temporary funding gap until a specified repayment event. The actual facility can differ significantly between a property-backed transaction, a short-term trading requirement and a business waiting for further investment. The exit must be assessed, not simply anticipated.
definitionHeading: A temporary need needs a clear way out.
benefits: Manage a mismatch in timing
Explore a defined gap where a payment is due before an identifiable cash receipt.
Support a transaction
Discuss temporary capital for a purchase or transition while a longer-term arrangement is progressed.
Consider the alternatives early
A bridge may fit a temporary need; an ongoing shortfall may need longer-term borrowing, equity or a different plan.

rows: Property purchase before a sale or refinance
Security, valuation and an evidenced exit
Trading purpose, repayment cash and available security

scenario.title: The purchase date comes before the expected receipt.
scenario.body: A business has a time-sensitive purchase and expects funds from a separate transaction. A short-term requirement is assessed around the evidence for that receipt, any security and the cost of a delay. The expected date alone does not establish that a bridge is available.
scenario.takeaway: The important question is not just how to obtain the cash, but how the business would repay if the expected event changed.

title: Property Finance
headline: Finance the property. Move the business forward.
intro: Buy business premises, refinance an existing property or fund the next development. Bring the asset and the plan to a conversation about the funding behind it.
uses: Buy premises or investment property
Explore commercial mortgages around the property, intended use, deposit and repayment source.
Fund a development
Set out acquisition costs, permissions, build stages, contingency and the proposed sale or refinance.
Refinance a property
Review existing borrowing or an equity-release requirement alongside valuation, charges and the replacement terms.
steps: Set out the asset
Share the property type, intended use, purchase or current value and existing debt.
Cost the project
Separate purchase, works, professional costs, contingency and the contribution available.
Test the funding and exit
Review drawdown conditions, repayment source and the impact of delays before committing.
terms: Usable funds and your contribution
Clarify the net funds available after costs, the equity contribution and which costs must be met before or alongside lender funds.
Drawdowns and conditions
Understand valuation, monitoring, legal and other conditions, including when money can actually be released.
Interest and fees
Consider the whole project cost, including arrangement, monitoring, legal and exit charges where applicable.
Term and exit
Test sales or refinance assumptions, contingency and what happens if delivery or sales take longer. An extension should not be assumed.
prepare: Property type, region and acquisition or project stage
Costs, equity, planning position and relevant experience
Required date, programme and proposed exit
faqs: Can funding complete by my deadline?
That depends on the asset, available information, valuation, legal work and the provider’s conditions. Share a real deadline early so the critical path can be considered.
How much equity will I need?
Requirements depend on the provider, asset and project. A single published lender limit is not a universal rule.
Can I refinance a completed development?
A development exit or other refinance may be a relevant conversation, subject to the property, existing borrowing, timing and a credible exit.
valueHeading: Put the asset, costs and exit in one picture.
valueIntro: We help distinguish the property funding requirement from the wider business costs, organise the initial case and arrange relevant introductions. Legal, valuation and other specialist work remains with the appropriate professionals.
enquiryHeading: What are your plans for the property?
enquiryIntro: Share the property type, broad funding requirement, current stage and any real deadline. An address or confidential pack is not needed to start.
definition: Property finance provides borrowing linked to a property and its intended use. A commercial mortgage, development facility and short-term bridge serve different stages: buying or holding an asset, delivering a project, or covering a temporary gap before an exit.
benefitsHeading: Build the property plan around the right structure.
benefits: Acquire premises
Explore finance for a depot, workshop, office or other eligible business property rather than funding the whole purchase from available cash.
Review an existing asset
Consider refinancing around current debt, valuation, available equity and the purpose of any additional funds.
Deliver a development
Connect land and build costs with permissions, staged funding, contingency and the expected sale or refinance.
assets: Development and refurbishment requirements, assessed around the project

scenario.takeaway: A development with a sale exit is a different requirement from premises held for long-term business use.

title: Equity & Growth Capital
headline: Capital for growth. A partner for the next chapter.
intro: Expand the business, make an acquisition or plan an ownership transition. Explore equity around the opportunity, the people involved and the future you want to build.
summary: Equity investment for growth and ownership change.
uses: Capital into the business
Set out the expansion or acquisition plan and what new investment should enable.
Liquidity for shareholders
Separate a shareholder sale from capital available to fund the company’s next plans.
A management or ownership transaction
Frame the buyout, acquisition or succession objective around management and shareholder alignment.
steps: Agree the objective
Clarify growth capital, shareholder proceeds and the type of partner sought.
Prepare the proposition
Bring commercial evidence, financial forecasts and ownership information into a coherent investment case.
Review the full terms
Assess valuation, rights, conditions and alignment alongside the amount invested.
terms: Valuation and dilution
Understand the ownership being issued or transferred, how proceeds are used and the effect on existing shareholders.
Governance and control
Board roles, consent rights and other terms can affect decisions even in a minority investment.
Investor alignment
Sector, strategy, management expectations and future funding capacity need to fit the plan.
Process and exit
Diligence and shareholder agreement take time. Clarify the investor’s horizon and expectations about future liquidity.
prepare: The intended split between company investment and shareholder proceeds
Current ownership, management involvement and the decisions shareholders can support
Capital purpose, timetable, financial picture and existing advisers
faqs: Does equity always mean selling control?
No, but minority ownership does not mean an absence of governance rights. The proposed terms need specific review.
Is the highest valuation the best offer?
The full agreement matters: governance, conditions, incentives, investor fit and exit expectations can change the overall assessment.
Will my information be circulated to investors?
The scope of any introduction and information sharing should be agreed. A first conversation does not require sending a shareholder register or confidential pack.
valueHeading: Connect the commercial opportunity with shareholder priorities.
valueIntro: We help frame the use of funds and the ownership objectives before arranging relevant capital introductions. Investor materials, models and ownership scenarios can be commissioned separately where preparation is needed.
enquiryHeading: What would the right capital partner help you achieve?
enquiryIntro: Share the business stage, growth or ownership objective and broad capital need. We can start without a valuation or confidential investor pack.
definition: Equity funding gives an investor an ownership interest in return for capital. New shares can fund the company; a sale of existing shares can provide liquidity to shareholders. Some transactions combine both, so where the money goes matters as much as the headline valuation.
definitionHeading: Investment changes both capital and ownership.
benefitsHeading: Fund the next chapter with ownership in view.
benefits: Back an ambitious growth plan
Support expansion or acquisition with capital that has a different commitment from scheduled loan repayments.
Plan an ownership transition
Separate money for the business from proceeds for shareholders, succession or a management transaction.
Assess partner fit
Look beyond price to strategy, governance, future funding capacity and expectations for an eventual exit.

rows: Into the company through new shares
Use of funds, dilution and growth plan
To the company and selling owners
Balance of growth funding, liquidity and governance

stepsHeading: Build an investment case and an ownership plan.

scenario.title: Growth funding and shareholder proceeds are not the same.
scenario.body: An established business wants to expand while one shareholder seeks a partial exit. The proposed transaction separates new investment available to the company from the purchase of existing shares. The management plan and governance need to work for both parts.
scenario.takeaway: A headline investment amount does not tell you how much cash will be available to fund the business.

title: Venture Funding
headline: Fund the milestone that moves the company forward.
intro: Build the product, prove demand or scale from commercial traction. Shape the funding round around what needs to be achieved and the evidence behind the opportunity.
uses: Validate the proposition
Define what still needs proving, the test or customer evidence sought and the cost to reach that point.
Prepare the funding round
Align the milestone, investor proposition, use of proceeds and existing round status.
Scale from commercial evidence
Show how capital supports delivery or growth, with unit economics, cash burn and later funding in view.
steps: Define the milestone
Specify what the capital will achieve and how progress can be measured.
Build the evidence
Align the pitch, forecast, use of funds and ownership position.
Target the right conversation
Consider investor mandate and stage before an agreed introduction, then prepare for diligence and terms.
terms: Stage and investor mandate
Evidence appropriate to the round is more useful than a broad list of investors.
Ownership and rights
Compare dilution with preferences, governance, incentives and future rounds.
Runway and milestones
Allow for delays and future capital requirements. A milestone is not a guaranteed valuation increase.
Readiness and execution
Decks, forecasts, ownership and diligence need to tell a coherent story; a raise cannot be guaranteed.
prepare: Stage, customer or technical evidence and what remains unproven
The milestone, costed use of proceeds and runway to reach it
Current round status, existing investor discussions and future capital needs
faqs: Can a pre-revenue business raise capital?
Some investors consider early-stage risk, but the stage, evidence, opportunity and mandate must fit. Pre-revenue status alone does not establish suitability.
Can debt avoid dilution?
Some venture debt includes warrants and other commitments, alongside repayment. Compare the actual terms rather than assuming zero dilution.
Do I need to upload a pitch deck immediately?
No. A non-confidential summary can establish the initial context before agreeing whether and how more detailed material should be shared.
valueHeading: Make the investment story stand up to the numbers.
valueIntro: We help clarify the round, stage and use of proceeds before relevant investor conversations. Where needed, financial modelling and investor materials are separate advisory engagements with agreed deliverables.
enquiryHeading: What milestone are you raising capital to reach?
enquiryIntro: Tell us what the company does, its stage and the broad round objective. There is no need to upload a deck for the first conversation.
definition: Venture funding backs companies with potential for significant growth, usually in exchange for equity or another agreed investment instrument. It is not simply a loan alternative: investors assess the opportunity, team, progress and potential return alongside the funding requirement.
definitionHeading: What would the next round make possible?
benefitsHeading: Connect capital with a meaningful next milestone.
benefits: Develop and validate
Set out what the product or market still needs to prove and what it will cost to reach that evidence.
Turn traction into scale
Explain how capital supports sales, delivery, people or market expansion, with unit economics and operating capacity in view.
Plan beyond the raise
Model runway, dilution and what happens if the next milestone takes longer to reach.

rows: Team, problem, product progress and initial customer evidence
What must the first capital prove?
Customer adoption, revenue quality and repeatability
Economics, capacity, retention and market opportunity
How much capital supports sustainable expansion?

scenario.title: More revenue is an outcome. The funding plan needs the detail.
scenario.body: A company raising to scale separates recruitment, product development, sales expenditure and delivery capacity. Its forecast shows the expected cash burn and time needed to test the growth assumptions. It also considers the runway if customer acquisition is slower.
scenario.takeaway: The funding amount should follow a costed milestone and cash plan, not only the valuation the founders hope to achieve.

title: Complex Funding
headline: A complex requirement deserves a clear starting point.
intro: A facility maturity, lender change, carve-out or unusual transaction can make a funding need harder to explain. We help bring the facts and next decisions into focus.
uses: Address a funding deadline
Set out a facility maturity, lender change or refinancing constraint and what must happen next.
Navigate a complex transaction
Explain the acquisition, carve-out or unusual structure and the stakeholders who need to agree.
Assess funding through change
Connect a credible operating plan with the immediate constraints and existing obligations.
steps: Establish the facts
Describe what changed, why capital is needed and the real timing.
Map the constraints
Identify borrowing, security, stakeholders and any professional input required.
Agree a focused route
Determine whether preparation, a provider introduction or a specialist adviser is the appropriate next action.
terms: Viability before capital
Explain how the plan addresses the underlying issue rather than postponing it.
Stakeholder alignment
Existing lenders, shareholders and advisers may need to agree before a transaction can proceed.
Cost and priority
New capital can bring significant cost, security and conditions. These require candid assessment.
Timing and discretion
Share the real deadline and agree information handling. Do not assume immediate availability or absolute confidentiality.
prepare: What changed, what must happen next and any real deadline
A broad description of the plan, repayment or exit and existing obligations
The stakeholders, advisers and consents involved
faqs: Can funding solve every difficult situation?
No. Viability, professional advice and stakeholder decisions can matter before a capital route is considered.
Should I include detailed creditor information in an enquiry?
Start with a broad, non-sensitive summary. Agree a suitable secure process before sending detailed financial or legal material.
How quickly can the situation be assessed?
That depends on the information, complexity and actual specialist availability. A deadline is important context, not a guarantee of funding by that date.
valueHeading: Make the requirement understandable before it is circulated.
valueIntro: We help organise the business case and dependencies, then identify relevant funding conversations where there is a realistic basis to proceed. Insolvency, enforcement or director-duty issues require appropriately qualified professional advice.
enquiryHeading: What has changed, and what needs to happen next?
enquiryIntro: Share a short outline and any real deadline. Keep creditor, legal and other confidential documents for an agreed later exchange.
definition: Complex funding describes a situation rather than one product. The eventual route might involve refinancing, asset-backed lending, acquisition finance or other capital. Start with the business need, deadline, existing obligations and decisions that have to be resolved.
definitionHeading: Name the situation before choosing the structure.
benefitsHeading: Bring order to a requirement with moving parts.
benefits: Respond to a funding change
Set out a maturity, reduced facility or proposed lender change while there is time to assess the options.
Navigate a transaction
Identify the capital need within an acquisition, carve-out or structure involving several stakeholders.
Focus the next action
Separate missing information, consents and professional advice from the funding itself.

title: Technology Finance
headline: Invest in better technology. Keep capital working elsewhere.
intro: Upgrade equipment, modernise systems or deliver an automation project. Explore funding around the technology investment, implementation plan and cash the business needs to retain.
summary: Equipment, software and implementation for operating businesses.
uses: Equipment and automation
Define the asset, supplier, delivery and commissioning requirements.
Software and implementation
Separate licences, integration, training and ongoing service costs; eligibility depends on the actual facility.
Raising capital for a technology company?
Company fundraising belongs with stage, traction, ownership and runway—not an equipment purchase assessment.
steps: Break down the quote
Identify hardware, licences, implementation and ongoing support as separate lines.
Test the project timetable
Plan installation, adoption and cash generation alongside payment commitments.
Compare the relevant structures
Review ownership, term, eligible costs and the impact on the business’s cash headroom.
terms: Eligible expenditure
Confirm what is actually financeable, including deposits, software, integration and service costs.
Delivery and repayment
Match commitments to installation, adoption and the timing of benefits; do not assume immediate savings.
Ownership and obligations
Clarify ownership or end-of-term options for assets and the conditions of any borrowing.
Company capital
A startup round introduces different ownership, investor and runway considerations from equipment finance.
prepare: The asset or capability, supplier quote and cost categories
Delivery, installation, training and expected productive-use dates
Commercial assumptions, existing obligations and repayment source
faqs: Can software and implementation costs be funded?
That depends on the product and provider. A quote should separate equipment, software, services and implementation so the scope can be assessed.
Will savings cover the repayments?
That is a business-case assumption to test, including delays and downside scenarios. Finance does not guarantee the expected return.
We are a technology startup. Which route should we use?
Start with the company’s stage and capital purpose. The venture or growth-capital journey may be more relevant than an equipment-finance discussion.
valueHeading: Bring the funding discussion back to the actual investment.
valueIntro: We help break down the expenditure and repayment case before exploring relevant introductions. The aim is a clear funding requirement for the operating project, with any separate modelling or preparation work agreed in advance.
enquiryHeading: What technology investment are you planning?
enquiryIntro: Tell us the project, approximate cost and timing. A supplier quote can follow once we have agreed the scope of the discussion.
definition: Technology finance supports an operating business investing in eligible technology assets. Hardware, software, integration and ongoing services are different cost categories; they should be separated so the appropriate asset-finance or business-borrowing route can be assessed.
definitionHeading: Fund the capability your business is buying.
benefitsHeading: Make the investment work for the operating business.
benefits: Modernise without one large cash outlay
Explore spreading eligible expenditure instead of using the full purchase amount from working capital.
Plan a replacement cycle
Compare ownership and leasing around the useful life, support needs and refresh plans for the equipment.
Budget for implementation
Include installation, training and the transition period in the business case even where those costs need separate funding.
assets: Computers, servers and other identifiable IT hardware
Production technology, automation and specialist equipment
A separately assessed software or systems investment

rows: Own it or lease it, and for how long?
Which costs are eligible and how will they generate repayment cash?
A separately assessed business funding requirement
Is the money for the company’s runway rather than a purchase?

scenario.body: A business replaces ageing infrastructure as part of a wider systems project. It separates equipment, software, migration and training. The funding discussion considers which costs a provider can support while the cash forecast allows for implementation and a period of overlap.
scenario.takeaway: Do not assume every item in a project quote is financed under the same agreement or that savings begin immediately.

title: Sustainability & Impact
headline: Fund cleaner operations and purposeful growth.
intro: Invest in more efficient equipment or grow a business with an environmental or social purpose. Start with the investment you want to make and the commercial case behind it.
uses: Improve your operations
Cost an efficiency or cleaner-equipment investment alongside installation and delivery assumptions.
Grow an impact-led business
Connect the growth model, capital requirement and intended environmental or social outcome.
Define the evidence
Identify the baseline, measurement method and what the investment could reasonably change.
steps: Cost the requirement
Separate assets, implementation, operating costs and contingency.
Assess the commercial case
Test repayment or investment assumptions as well as the intended improvement.
Agree proportionate evidence
Identify what needs to be measured and any actual provider reporting conditions.
terms: Commercial viability
Test the investment economics and delivery assumptions alongside the intended benefit.
Evidence and reporting
Clarify the baseline, measurement method and any provider-specific reporting obligations.
Actual product terms
Environmental purpose does not guarantee lower cost, a grant or preferential eligibility.
Delivery of outcomes
Be explicit about dependencies and uncertainty; avoid claims that the funding alone proves impact.
prepare: Operational investment or business-growth purpose and the costed plan
The baseline and intended environmental or social outcome
Delivery assumptions, measurement method and commercial evidence
faqs: Will sustainable finance be cheaper?
Not necessarily. Compare the actual product, terms, requirements and total cost rather than assuming a green label changes the price.
Is grant funding included?
Availability and support for grants must be confirmed separately. This page does not promise a grant or assume that a project qualifies.
Do we need formal impact reporting?
Requirements vary by route and provider. Measurement should be appropriate to the intended outcome and any actual funding conditions.
valueHeading: Connect the investment, the commercial case and the intended change.
valueIntro: We help distinguish an asset project from company growth capital and organise the information for a relevant introduction. Technical assessment and any independent evidence of savings remain separate specialist work.
primaryCta: Discuss your investment or impact plan
enquiryHeading: What investment or impact-led growth plan are you considering?
enquiryIntro: Tell us what you want to fund, the approximate cost and the intended improvement. We will start with the practical requirement.
definition: Sustainable investment and impact-led company funding are different requirements. One may involve equipment or property expenditure; the other may involve equity or business borrowing to grow a company. The funding structure should follow the actual use of money, not the label alone.
benefitsHeading: Make the intended improvement a fundable business plan.
benefits: Invest in operating assets
Explore funding for eligible cleaner equipment, energy-related assets or efficiency projects, with installation and running costs in view.
Build the commercial case
Compare upfront expenditure with realistic operating assumptions and an achievable delivery plan.
Grow an impact-led business
Connect the business model, capital requirement and intended outcomes with the appropriate debt or investment conversation.
assets: Company growth with a defined environmental or social purpose

rows: Asset finance or other suitable borrowing
Commercial model, use of funds and intended outcomes
Measurement rather than a separate funding product
Baseline, assumptions and evidence of what changed

scenario.body: A business considers solar and storage for its premises. The business case includes equipment, installation, site requirements and operating assumptions. The funding discussion assesses the actual investment; the model tests a range of output, usage and price assumptions.
scenario.takeaway: Finance does not itself prove savings or impact. Grants, discounts and specific technical outcomes are not assumed.
